recent_articles.title: Govt plans Wapda security force for water projects - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Pakistani government** has decided to create a new "Wapda Security Force" to provide dedicated security to major water sector infrastructure projects and workers, particularly those from China. The force will be created through the Wapda Security Force Act, 2026, following two terrorist attacks on engineers and workers at the Dasu Hydropower Project in 2021 and 2024.  The new force will operate across the country with its own uniform, insignia, and stamp, providing security to dams, power plants, machinery, equipment, offices, personnel, and residences of personnel working on Wapda projects. The force's strength will depend on security requirements.

recent_articles.title: Scotland’s ‘green datacentres’ policy ignores emissions impact of AI, analysis shows | Scotland | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A Scottish charity, **Action to Protect Rural Scotland (APRS)**, has raised concerns that a government policy encouraging the development of "green datacenters" could lead to significant carbon emissions being ignored.  **Ariane Burgess**, a **Green MSP**, argues for transparency regarding what constitutes a "green datacenter" and how their energy demands will be met by the grid infrastructure. APRS found that some datacenters are claiming to be green while having substantial emissions, potentially receiving favorable treatment from local authorities. The Scottish government acknowledges Scotland's strengths as a location for green datacenters but emphasizes its commitment to aligning these projects with net zero ambitions and community benefits.
